news.title: Ghana knocked out of 2026 WAFCON quarter-finals by debutants Malawi
news.lede: The result also doubles as a historic qualification to the 2027 Women's World Cup for WAFCON debutants Malawi. Ghana and Malawi had previously faced off in a pre-tournament friendly just weeks prior with the Black Queens easily winning 4-0. However, it was always going to be a different encouter this time especially after the Scorchers topped Group C with Nigeria, Zambia, and Egypt. It was a dream start for Kim Lars Bjorkegren's women after Chantelle Boye Hlorkah volleyed home just 7 minutes into the game to give Ghana the lead after seven minutes.

news.title: WAFCON 2026 — Cameroon, Malawi clinch semifinal, FIFA World Cup spots on day of upsets
news.lede: Getty Images Getty Images https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/go1mwn/article71326901.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/toolxox.com-free-ai-tools-3k-WtoZzknVTR.jpg All four semifinalists qualify automatically for the tournament in Brazil, while Nigeria and the other losing quarterfinal teams play on Thursday with two spots in an intercontinental playoff tournament up for grabs. CASABLANCA Cameroon shocked defending champion Nigeria and Malawi stunned Ghana to reach the semifinals of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Sunday and seal World Cup qualification. Cameroon goalkeeper Michaely Bihina excelled and her team held on as the 19-year-old Myriam Nyadjou’s early goal was enough for the Indomitable Lionesses’ 1-0 win over 10-time champion Nigeria. It is the first time that Nigeria has failed to reach the semifinals, where Cameroon will face host nation Morocco on Wednesday.

news.title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour

news.title: ‘It’s a true art form’: Nigeria goalkeeper Maduka Okoye on high fashion and life at Udinese
news.lede: The former Watford player talks about his off-field pursuits, lessons from the World Cup and unfinished business. When Maduka Okoye visited Paris fashion week for the Jean Paul Gaultier show, taking his seat in the front row alongside rapper Cardi B, the online reaction was swift. Within hours, footage of the Udinese and Nigeria goalkeeper was all over TikTok and Instagram – where his audience now stretches to nearly two million followers – transforming the appearance into a viral cultural moment that crossed beyond the boundaries of football. Yet ask Okoye to reflect on his sudden explosion into the fashion ecosystem, and he frames it not as a pursuit of celebrity or status, but as a genuine interest in art.
